title: Insider Trading and Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.description: Collective term for Company Persons (Board, officers, employees of Anteris and subsidiaries, and other persons the Company determines, e.g. contractors, consultants or stockholders with access to Material Nonpublic Information), Family Members and Controlled Entities. Subject to the core Prohibited Transactions rules: no trading on MNPI, no short sales, no exchange-traded put/call options, no hedging or monetisation, and no pledging of Company Securities as loan collateral.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Company's Board of Directors. Subject to Section 16 Reports, Form 144 filings, ASX notification of interests within 2 business days, and (as officers/directors) a longer 90-120 day Rule 10b5-1 cooling-off period.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors, executive officers, legal department members, regional/executive management or corporate support employees, clinical trial staff, individuals reporting to the CFO, financial-statement preparers, employees with forecast knowledge, designated Investor Relations professionals, anyone with MNPI access via the foregoing, other persons designated by the CEO/CFO/General Counsel, and their Family Members and Controlled Entities. Subject to Pre-Clearance Procedures and Quarterly Blackout Periods.

definitions.hedging_definition: transactions that hedge or offset, or are designed to hedge or offset, any decrease in the market value of Company Securities, accomplished through mechanisms including prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, collars and exchange funds

windows.start_anchor: first day of the last month of each fiscal quarter (March 1st, June 1st, September 1st and December 1st)
windows.end_anchor: beginning of the third business day following the date of the public release of the Company's earnings results for that quarter

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer or General Counsel may designate an event-specific trading restriction period, or accelerate/extend a Blackout Period, without disclosing the reason; its existence is not announced to the Company as a whole and must not be communicated to any other person, and exceptions will not be granted during it.

rules.detail: Exchange-traded or organized-market put options, call options or other derivative securities over Company Securities are expressly banned for all Insiders, with no clearance route.
rules.evidence: transactions in put options, call options or other derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organized market, are prohibited by this Policy.

rules.detail: The exchange/organized-market derivatives ban does not by its terms reach an OTC put or call, but the Hedging Transactions clause independently and expressly bans 'collars' as a hedging mechanism regardless of venue, so an OTC put/call collar is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: Hedging or monetization transactions can be accomplished through a number of possible mechanisms, including through the use of financial instruments such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, collars and exchange funds ... Accordingly, hedging transactions by any Insider, or any of their designees, are prohibited under this Policy.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging transactions by any Insider or their designees, expressly naming prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, collars and exchange funds as examples. Applies regardless of whether the securities were obtained through an employee benefit plan or otherwise, and with no vesting-state distinction or clearance carve-out.
rules.evidence: Hedging or monetization transactions can be accomplished through a number of possible mechanisms, including through the use of financial instruments such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, collars and exchange funds ... Accordingly, hedging transactions by any Insider, or any of their designees, are prohibited under this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation transactions are named alongside hedging transactions in the same heading and prohibited on the same terms, with prepaid variable forwards and equity swaps given as examples.
rules.evidence: Hedging or monetization transactions can be accomplished through a number of possible mechanisms, including through the use of financial instruments such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, collars and exchange funds.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short sales of Company Securities for all Insiders; Section 16(c) of the Exchange Act separately bans officers and directors from short selling.
rules.evidence: short sales of Company Securities are prohibited. In addition, Section 16(c) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act") prohibits officers and directors from engaging in short sales of Company securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
A CFD-equivalent exposure is expressly named as 'equity swaps' within the prohibited hedging mechanisms, independent of venue.
rules.evidence: including through the use of financial instruments such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, collars and exchange funds.

rules.detail: Insiders are absolutely prohibited from holding Company Securities in a margin account as collateral for a margin loan, with no Company consent or clearance carve-out.
rules.evidence: Insiders are prohibited from pledging, hypothecating or otherwise using Company Securities as collateral for a loan or other form of indebtedness, including, without limitation, holding Company Securities in a margin account as collateral for a margin loan.

rules.detail: Pledging, hypothecating or otherwise using Company Securities as collateral for any loan or indebtedness is banned outright for all Insiders, with no exception for the purpose or lender involved.
rules.evidence: Insiders are prohibited from pledging, hypothecating or otherwise using Company Securities as collateral for a loan or other form of indebtedness.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on using Company Securities as collateral for any loan or other form of indebtedness, not limited to margin loans; no clearance route or exemption authority exists for this prohibition.
rules.evidence: Insiders are prohibited from pledging, hypothecating or otherwise using Company Securities as collateral for a loan or other form of indebtedness, including, without limitation, holding Company Securities in a margin account as collateral for a margin loan.

rules.detail: The Policy itself imposes no minimum holding period or short-term/speculative trading restriction. Exhibit A separately notes that Section 16(b) of the Exchange Act can require directors and officers to disgorge short-swing profits from opposite-way transactions within six months, a statutory consequence rather than a Policy-imposed rule.

clearance.approver: Chief Financial Officer or General Counsel
clearance.evidence: The Company is under no obligation to approve a transaction submitted for pre-clearance and may determine not to permit the transaction. ... If permission to engage in the transaction is granted, then the transaction must be initiated within five business days of receipt of pre-clearance ... in which case the preclearance is void and the trade must not be completed.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (for ASX purposes); General Counsel's office or CFO (for Section 16 Reports); broker (for Form 144)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 2 business days after a change occurs (to Company Secretary); before the end of the second business day following the trade (Form 4); before an open market sale (Form 144)
clearance.evidence: Within 2 business days after a change occurs, a Director must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the requisite information for the Company Secretary to make the necessary notifications to ASX as required by the ASX Listing Rules.

exceptions.evidence: This Policy does not apply to the exercise of employee stock options (where no shares of stock are sold to fund the exercise), or when shares are withheld by Anteris for the Company Person's payment of withholding taxes or the applicable exercise price upon exercise (if authorized by the Company).

This Policy does not apply to the vesting of restricted stock and restricted stock units under Anteris' equity plans, or when related shares or units are withheld by Anteris for the Company Person to pay withholding taxes upon vesting (if authorized by the Company).

This Policy does not apply to purchases of Company Securities in the Company's employee stock purchase plan, 401(k) plan, or deferred compensation plans or similar employee benefit plans resulting from a Company Person's periodic contribution of money to the plan pursuant to his or her payroll deduction election.

This Policy does not apply to purchases of Company Securities under a Company or a broker-sponsored dividend reinvestment plan resulting from a Company Person's reinvestment of dividends paid on Company Securities.
Any other purchase of Company Securities from Anteris or sales of Company Securities to Anteris are not subject to this Policy.

Bona fide gifts of Company Securities to a family member, charitable organization, or any other person (including a transfer to a family trust) are not transactions subject to this Policy, unless the person making the gift has reason to believe that the recipient intends to sell the Company Securities while the person making the gift is aware of Material Nonpublic Information

Transactions in a mutual fund or other collective investment vehicle (e.g., hedge fund or exchange traded fund) that is invested in Company Securities and (1) is publicly traded and widely held, (2) is broad based and diversified, and (3) has investment discretion for fund investments exercised by an independent third party are not transactions subject to this Policy.

exceptions.approver: Chief Financial Officer or General Counsel
exceptions.evidence: To comply with this Policy, Trading Plans must be approved by the Chief Financial Officer or the General Counsel (if any) and must be adopted in accordance with the guidelines applicable to Trading Plans attached as Exhibit A hereto.

exemption_authority: No hardship or discretionary exemption exists for the short sale, exchange-traded options, hedging/monetisation or margin/pledging prohibitions in section 4.B. The only routes to trade are the enumerated Permitted Transactions in section 4.C (non-market plan mechanics) and Rule 10b5-1 Trading Plans approved by the CFO or General Counsel, neither of which overrides these substantive prohibitions.
jurisdiction_overlays: US Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Section 16, Section 16(b) short-swing profit recovery, Rule 10b5-1)
Australian Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) section 1043A insider trading

bespoke_clauses.topic: collars named as prohibited hedging mechanism
bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging or monetization transactions can be accomplished through a number of possible mechanisms, including through the use of financial instruments such as prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, collars and exchange funds.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy expressly names 'collars' as a prohibited hedging mechanism, so the exact structure proposed (purchased put + written call) is unambiguously banned regardless of venue or vesting status.

bespoke_clauses.topic: exchange-traded derivatives ban limited by venue
bespoke_clauses.clause: transactions in put options, call options or other derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organized market, are prohibited by this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This specific ban is textually limited to exchange/organized-market derivatives; an OTC derivative escapes it, but is independently caught by the venue-agnostic hedging ban naming collars, so the venue limitation provides no path around the prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Insiders are prohibited from pledging, hypothecating or otherwise using Company Securities as collateral for a loan or other form of indebtedness.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This bars the secured loan leg of a funded collar regardless of the lender or structure, with no company-consent carve-out, unlike some ASX policies that permit pledging with clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy continues to apply to transactions in Company Securities even after termination of service to, or employment with, the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A departing director or executive cannot use termination of service to escape the hedging or pledging bans while still restricted or in possession of MNPI.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Trading Plan entered into or modified by a member of the board of directors or an executive officer of the Company must include a cooling-off period of at least the later of: (i) 90 days after the adoption or modification of the Trading Plan and (ii) two business days following the disclosure of the Company's financial results ... such cooling-off period need not exceed 120 days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the substantive hedging/pledging bans were waived, the policy's only trading safe-harbour (a 10b5-1 plan) could not be used to execute an immediate collar; it requires a 90-120 day cooling-off before any trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: these exceptions may not provide a defence to insider trading liability under Australian securities laws – you must ensure that you comply with all applicable laws in relation to such Permitted Transactions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a transaction structured to fit a Policy exception, or a Rule 10b5-1 plan, gives no protection under Australian insider trading law, so a bank's Australian law exposure around the collar needs independent analysis.

summary: A funded collar with a bank is expressly and comprehensively prohibited under this policy. Section 4.B.iii bans hedging or monetisation transactions by any Insider, naming 'collars' (together with prepaid variable forwards and equity swaps) as a specifically prohibited mechanism, with no clearance route, vesting-state exception or approved-plan carve-out. Section 4.B.iv independently bans pledging, hypothecating or otherwise using Company Securities as collateral for any loan or other indebtedness, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is also banned outright regardless of lender or structure. The narrower ban on exchange-traded put/call options (4.B.ii) would not by its terms reach an OTC structure, but this makes no difference because the collar-naming hedging ban and the margin/pledge ban both apply irrespective of venue. Rule 10b5-1 plans, the policy's only recognised trading safe-harbour, cannot substitute for a collar given their mandatory 90-to-120-day cooling-off period and their inability to override these substantive prohibitions. There is no hardship exception or discretionary waiver anywhere in the policy for the hedging or pledging bans, so no structuring path exists for a bank-funded collar.
